goals.label: Prepare for an interview
goals.summary: Practise the concepts and explain your reasoning.

routes.label: Market risk & FRTB
routes.title: Explain how market risk becomes capital.
routes.intro: Build the intuition, follow the calculation and practise explaining the assumptions behind the result.

steps.title: Build your risk vocabulary
steps.detail: Use delta, vega and curvature to explain how a position responds to market moves.

steps.title: Connect sensitivities to capital
steps.detail: Work through FRTB SA and IMA, then explain aggregation, diversification and model checks.

steps.title: Discuss the implementation context
steps.detail: Compare the FRTB frameworks and explain why jurisdiction and rule status matter.

routes.reason: FRTB interview questions, worked cases and revision flashcards help you turn the calculations into clear explanations.
routes.practice: Explain one capital calculation aloud, including its inputs, assumptions and a limitation.

routes.label: Credit risk
routes.title: Explain what drives a credit loss.
routes.intro: Follow three focused lessons in the Credit Risk module, then practise defending the assumptions in a worked case.

steps.title: Connect PD, LGD and EAD
steps.detail: Start with the portfolio loss explorer and explain the ingredients of expected loss.

steps.title: Stress the portfolio
steps.detail: Explore default dependence and explain why losses can cluster in stressed conditions.

steps.title: Distinguish loss and capital
steps.detail: Compare accounting loss, provisions and capital, and explain what each measure tells you.

routes.reason: Credit-risk worked cases, interview practice and flashcards support revision of loss drivers, modelling choices and practical explanations.
routes.practice: Walk through a credit-loss example and explain which assumption most changes the result.

routes.label: Counterparty risk & XVA
routes.title: Follow a trade from exposure to valuation.
routes.intro: Build a coherent explanation of exposure, counterparty credit risk and the adjustments used in pricing.

steps.title: Understand counterparty exposure
steps.detail: Explore replacement cost, potential future exposure, netting and collateral.

steps.title: Connect exposure to CVA risk
steps.detail: Study counterparty credit effects and the sensitivities used in SA-CVA.

steps.title: Explain the valuation adjustments
steps.detail: Connect credit, funding, collateral and capital costs to the economics of a trade.

routes.reason: The XVA guide and worked cases help you connect the adjustments, while interview questions and flashcards support structured practice.
routes.practice: Explain how collateral changes exposure and funding, then describe the effect on a trade's valuation.

routes.label: Treasury & ALM
routes.title: Explain a bank's funding and rate-risk decisions.
routes.intro: Start with the balance sheet, trace the cash needs and connect rate shocks to earnings and economic value.

steps.title: Understand the balance sheet
steps.detail: Explain funding needs, net interest income and the role of funds transfer pricing.

steps.title: Follow the cash under stress
steps.detail: Explore LCR, NSFR and cash survival, then discuss possible funding actions.

steps.title: Explain banking-book rate risk
steps.detail: Connect yield-curve shocks, deposit behaviour and hedges to EVE and NII.

routes.reason: Treasury worked cases and interview questions help you practise explaining funding, liquidity and balance-sheet decisions together.
routes.practice: Present one treasury decision, its effect on earnings and liquidity, and the trade-off you would discuss with ALCO.

goals.label: Build practical modelling knowledge
goals.summary: Build a curve, test the risks and explain the result.

routes.label: Practical modelling
routes.title: Build from valuation inputs to model behaviour.
routes.intro: Begin with discounting and a hands-on curve workflow, then explore sensitivities and the mathematics of uncertain prices.

steps.title: Build and test a yield curve
steps.detail: Bootstrap discount factors, infer forwards and check how the curve reprices bonds and swaps.

steps.title: Measure what moves the value
steps.detail: Change rates and other market inputs, compare price changes and interpret the sensitivities.

steps.title: Add the stochastic foundations
steps.detail: Explore probability, Brownian motion and Itô calculus. Refresh basic calculus before this step.

routes.reason: The Yield Curves package supports your first practical build with a structured guide, worked cases and an offline lab for repeated practice.
routes.practice: Reprice an instrument, change one curve assumption and explain the resulting value and risk.

goals.label: Develop treasury expertise
goals.summary: Connect the balance sheet, liquidity and rate risk.

routes.label: Treasury expertise
routes.title: Connect everyday treasury decisions.
routes.intro: Follow the balance sheet through funding, liquidity stress and interest-rate risk, with a practical decision at each stage.

steps.title: Build the treasury foundation
steps.detail: Explore the bank balance sheet, funding costs, net interest income and funds transfer pricing.

steps.title: Test liquidity and funding resilience
steps.detail: Work through liquidity ratios, cash survival, collateral and funding concentration.

steps.title: Manage banking-book rate risk
steps.detail: Compare EVE and NII under rate shocks, then explore deposits, optionality and hedging.

routes.reason: The Treasury Risk package gives you a broad starting point, combining a professional guide, offline practice and worked treasury cases.
routes.practice: Use a worked balance-sheet case to explain a funding action and its effect on liquidity and net interest income.
